chain.label: FAA allowed generic Part 43 Appendix D inspection standards for former military turbine rotorcraft
chain.trigger: In December 2011, the FAA issued a Memorandum of Deviation to Order 8130.2G ... allowed former military turbine-powered rotorcraft with an experimental exhibition certificate, including the accident helicopter, to be inspected under the provisions of Appendix D to Title 14 Code of Federal Regulations Part 43.

chain.label: Operator did not submit the required annual program letter listing the June 2022 reunion event
chain.trigger: the FAA did not have a program letter or other correspondence from MARPAT Aviation indicating that the helicopter would be flown at the June 2022 annual event

chain.label: FAA performed no routine surveillance of the operator's experimental exhibition operation
chain.trigger: the FSDO had not performed surveillance of the operator (separate from its Part 145 repair station certificate) before the accident ... Order 8900.1 ... did not include a requirement for inspectors to perform routine surveillance of operators with experimental exhibition airworthiness certificates

caused_by.evidence: As a result, the Charleston FSDO was unaware that MARPAT Aviation was operating the accident helicopter at that event.

chain.label: Operator inspected the engine only to Appendix D minimums at annual intervals instead of the more rigorous, more frequent standards available to it
chain.trigger: the operator's failure to inspect the engine using more frequent inspection intervals and more rigorous standards readily available to the operator resulted in missed opportunities to potentially detect engine problems

caused_by.evidence: MARPAT Aviation performed inspections of the helicopter according to the generic inspection criteria for aircraft systems and components in Appendix D to 14 CFR Part 43, as required.
the FAA's inadequate oversight of the operator, which did not detect the inherent risk associated with the operation

chain.label: Undetected corrosion separation of the rear bearing cover outer flange and fatigue cracking of the exhaust diffuser inner cone and inner struts
chain.trigger: The rear bearing cover showed a pre-existing separation in the outer flange due to wall thinning from corrosion ... The cracks around the outer cone inner strut support flanges showed fatigue features from multiple origins

caused_by.evidence: the damage to the engine exhaust diffuser (cracking) and the rear bearing cover (outer flange separation) were significant long-term engine issues that could have been detected if the operator ... had used more detailed inspection criteria and more frequent inspection intervals

chain.label: Degraded radial support for the No. 3 and No. 4 bearings misaligned the power turbine shaft, causing rubbing against the rear compressor stub shaft
chain.trigger: The cracks in the exhaust diffuser led to reduced support for the No. 3 and No. 4 bearings, causing a misalignment in the power turbine shaft and rubbing on the power turbine blade shrouds.

caused_by.evidence: The reduced load transfer to the inner cone at the forward and aft ends of the bearing housing support likely led to increased stresses at the inner strut support attachments, resulting in cracks at the inner and outer flanges for the inner struts.

chain.label: No. 2 bearing failed from frictional heating and the engine lost power in flight
chain.trigger: the loss of engine power resulted from the failure of the No. 2 bearing; that failure occurred because of degraded radial support for the power turbine shaft at the No. 3 and No. 4 bearings

caused_by.evidence: The misalignment in the power turbine shaft led to rubbing with the rear compressor stub shaft, which resulted in frictional heating of the rear compressor stub shaft at the No. 2 bearing. The frictional heat then extended to the No. 2 bearing, causing it to fail.

chain.label: Helicopter struck two powerlines crossing the road during the autorotative forced landing
chain.trigger: the helicopter contacted powerlines during the forced landing

caused_by.evidence: The loss of engine power (discussed further in the next section) required an emergency autorotation and a forced landing.

chain.label: Pilot unable to maintain control after the powerline strike
chain.trigger: the pilot was unable to maintain control of the helicopter after it struck powerlines

caused_by.evidence: the helicopter contacted powerlines during the forced landing, which resulted in a loss of control

chain.label: Impact with rock face, road, and guardrail followed by postcrash fire
chain.trigger: The helicopter subsequently impacted the rock face, road, and guardrail near the bottom of the rock face. The guardrail impact likely caused the fuel tanks to rupture, which led to the postcrash fire.

caused_by.evidence: the pilot was unable to maintain control of the helicopter after it struck powerlines

chain.label: All six occupants fatally injured; helicopter destroyed
chain.trigger: The six helicopter occupants were fatally injured, and the helicopter was destroyed.

caused_by.evidence: Autopsies performed on all six helicopter occupants determined that their cause of death was blunt force and thermal injuries. The accident was not survivable.
